<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Be [...]
I’m using the `how` skill to place the rule in the existing lint architecture and the `verify-commands` skill to make the proposed checks meaningful. I’ll keep the investigation read-only.

command:
test -d .gitnexus && echo gitnexus-present || echo gitnexus-absent
printf '%s\n' '--- explainer prompt ---'
sed -n '1,300p' skills/pstack/how/references/explainer-prompt.md
printf '%s\n' '--- workspace model config ---'
if test -f .agents/pstack-models.md; then sed -n '1,240p' .agents/pstack-models.md; else echo absent; fi
printf '%s\n' '--- user model config ---'
if test -f "$HOME/.agents/pstack-models.md"; then sed -n '1,240p' "$HOME/.agents/pstack-models.md"; else echo absent; fi

git status --short
rg --files dev/lint tests .github | sed -n '1,240p'
rg -n "custom_lint|workspace_scoped_cache|disabled_rules_by_line|lint_no_|pre-commit" .pre-commit-config.yaml pyproject.toml dev tests .github 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,320p'

sed -n '1,260p' dev/lint/_framework.py
printf '%s\n' '--- custom_lint.py ---'
sed -n '1,260p' dev/lint/custom_lint.py
printf '%s\n' '--- lint_workspace_scoped_cache.py ---'
sed -n '1,340p' dev/lint/lint_workspace_scoped_cache.py
printf '%s\n' '--- workspace tests ---'
sed -n '1,280p' tests/dev/lint/test_lint_workspace_scoped_cache.py
printf '%s\n' '--- aggregate tests ---'
sed -n '1,220p' tests/dev/lint/test_custom_lint.py
printf '%s\n' '--- pre-commit relevant ---'
sed -n '1,90p' .pre-commit-config.yaml

sed -n '1,300p' dev/lint/lint_session_list_visibility.py
printf '%s\n' '--- session visibility tests ---'
sed -n '1,240p' tests/dev/lint/test_lint_session_list_visibility.py
printf '%s\n' '--- pyproject test config ---'
rg -n "\[tool.pytest|testpaths|pythonpath|addopts|dev/lint" pyproject.toml Justfile justfile 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,200p'

content.text: The existing runner already has the right extension point: one zero-argument `check()` per rule and no filenames from pre-commit. The new module should own both its aggregate path discovery and its explicit-file CLI; no new hook or shared framework abstraction is needed.

command:
pwd
ls -ld pyproject.toml tests/dev/lint dev/lint
if test -x .venv/bin/python; then echo .venv-python-present; else echo .venv-python-absent; fi
nl -ba dev/lint/custom_lint.py | sed -n '1,150p'
printf '%s\n' '--- framework lines ---'
nl -ba dev/lint/_framework.py | sed -n '1,120p'
printf '%s\n' '--- reference rule lines ---'
nl -ba dev/lint/lint_workspace_scoped_cache.py | sed -n '150,270p'
printf '%s\n' '--- hook lines ---'
nl -ba .pre-commit-config.yaml | sed -n '48,70p'

rg -n '^requires-python|target-version|python_version|python = ' pyproject.toml .python-version 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,120p'
rg -n '^type [A-Z][A-Za-z]+ =|TypeAlias' dev/lint omnigent tests/dev/lint | sed -n '1,100p'

for path in .venv/bin/pytest .venv/bin/pre-commit; do if test -x "$path"; then echo "$path present"; else echo "$path absent"; fi; done
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q tests/dev/lint/test_framework.py tests/dev/lint/test_custom_lint.py tests/dev/lint/test_lint_workspace_scoped_cache.py | tail -n 5

Keep the existing pre-commit hook unchanged. It already runs `python -m dev.lint.custom_lint` without filenames and expects each registered rule to own its scope ([custom_lint.py](/private/var/folders/xx/T/codex-ws-8ajtf0nh/dev/lint/custom_lint.py:6),  [...]
